chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadeed, from Jameel, from Zurara, who said:

I asked one of the two Imams (peace be upon him) about a man who led a group in prayer for two rak'ahs, then informed them that he had not been in a state of ablution. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The group completes their prayer, for there is no responsibility upon the Imam.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if an Imam leads prayer for two rak'ahs and then informs the congregation he was not in a state of ablution?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the principle of 'not imposing liability on the Imam' (laysa 'ala al-imam daman) when he leads prayer in a state of minor impurity or makes a counting error, ensuring the congregation's prayer remains valid. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the Imam's error does not invalidate the prayer for the followers, emphasizing the stability of congregational worship despite leadership imperfections. The ruling underscores the practical ease in Shia fiqh, prioritizing the continuity of the prayer over strict penalization of the Imam's mistake.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Jameel, from Zurara who said,

‘I asked one of the two (5th or 6th Imamasws about a man who prays with a group (leading them) in two Rak’at, so he informs them that he did not happen to be upon an ablution. Heasws said: ‘The group would complete their Salāt, for there is no responsibility upon the Imam’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Hadid from Jamil from Zurarah who has said the following: “

I once asked one of the two Imam, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, about a man who leads a people in Salah (prayer) of two Rak‘at and then informs them that he does not have a valid Wudu’. He (the Imam) said, ‘People must complete their Salah (prayer); there is no responsibility on Imam.’”
